dataset.name: automotive::generate_catalog(4500) split by index range into a 1500-product calibration slice and a 3000-product held-out slice, plus hand-built extension cases (collision, absent identifier, legitimate cross-reference, adversarial near-miss, 7-variant stress product); mixed_merchant's 3000-product mixed catalog retained separately for a future general-lexical-regression comparison

engine_config.note: none of these route through commerce_core::plan::execute_planned/LexicalDelegate -- LexicalHit cannot express a resolved VariantId at all, see ISSUE42_PROTOCOL.md's dated correction

repetitions: 5 independent full runs; every correctness/classification/recall/false-match/violation number is byte-identical across all 5 (confirmed by direct diff); latency, build time, incremental-update time, and RSS deltas vary run-to-run and are reported as ranges (including a disclosed bimodal split for Treatment B's incremental-update cost), not a single favorable run

headline_result.treatment_a: finds 0 of 2972 held-out identifiers -- part_number is variant-level only and phase9_eval::bitmap_delegate::build_index never indexes anything beyond product-level Text/title. Confirms H3-A.
headline_result.treatment_b: 100% Recall@1 / 0% false-match on the genuinely-unique held-out sample, correctly surfaces both variants of a deliberate collision, but matches a bare prefix query it should reject -- confirming H3-B's own predicted weakness directly.
headline_result.treatment_c: matches B's Recall@1/false-match numbers exactly (100%/0%) on the one field (part_number) it accepts, correctly rejects the prefix and adversarial near-miss queries, and builds/updates substantially faster than B in every one of 5 independent runs (build ~2.2-3.7ms vs B's ~12.1-13.2ms; incremental update ~0.0008-0.0027ms vs B's bimodal ~4.4-7.4ms/~104.5-107.4ms). Every other field present in the held-out catalog (17 of 18, including a deliberately-added 'legitimate cross-reference' field with only 2 occurrences sharing one value) correctly ABSTAINS, falling back to Treatment B exactly as the protocol's own abstention behavior requires. Confirms H3-C. PASSES every preregistered R3 GO-gate criterion.
headline_result.verdict: GO for Treatment C. Mirroring R2's own outcome (unlike R1's REVISE), Treatment C's calibrated-classifier-plus-dictionary mechanism clears every preregistered GO-gate criterion. Per Issue #42's own rule, this is a real candidate for a RED-before-GREEN production change to commerce_core -- deliberately not made in this same pass. A fresh, no-implementation-task adversarial reviewer must first attempt to falsify this protocol/fixture/code/arithmetic/claim and every confirmed finding independently reproduced and fixed, before that change is made; the production-change step itself is tracked separately (task #63, after R1/R2), so R1/R2/R3's serving-contract decisions are reviewed together.
headline_result.reproducibility: all 5 runs byte-identical on every correctness/classification/recall/false-match/violation number (verified by direct diff excluding the build_time_ms/incremental_update_ms/rss_delta_kb/index_size_bytes_b JSON fields)
headline_result.preregistration_corrections: Two found before any treatment code was written, both dated in ISSUE42_PROTOCOL.md: (1) automotive::generate_catalog has no seed parameter at all, so the protocol's literal calibration/held-out split text was unachievable, and a naive two-call workaround would have made calibration a byte-identical prefix of held-out -- fixed via one generate_catalog(4500) call split by index range into disjoint slices; (2) commerce_core::plan::LexicalHit has no VariantId field and verify_and_truncate's per-variant resolution is vacuously true whenever query.constraints is empty (exactly the identifier-only-query case, since compile() has no 'part number' keyword branch) -- so today's real pipeline always returns a product's first variant regardless of which variant matched; every R3 treatment is therefore its own self-contained index-and-lookup path with a real, variant-aware hit type instead.
headline_result.self_caught_methodology_bug: The initial Recall@1/false-match sample counted every naturally-occurring identifier collision (automotive's own real RNG draw occasionally repeating by chance, the same phenomenon the calibration set's own 0.998 uniqueness ratio already showed) as a false match whenever the sample iterated to one collision-partner and the top hit resolved to the other -- conflating a genuine, correctly-surfaced collision (separately tested and passing via the dedicated collision case) with an actual wrong resolution, producing an initial false read of 'Treatment C FAILS the GO gate' (0.37% false-match) purely from test-methodology, not a real defect. Fixed by excluding catalog-wide-non-unique identifiers (22 of 2994 candidates, disclosed) from the sample; both B and C then measure exactly 100%/0%. A second, unrelated determinism bug (shannon_entropy_bits summing floating-point terms in HashMap's randomized iteration order) was also self-caught by diffing 5 runs before trusting a byte-identical claim, and fixed via BTreeMap's deterministic order. Both caught and fixed before any adversarial review, following the same discipline R1/R2 established for self-caught bugs.
